subject: Secure telemetry exit strategies for private LLM deployments
messages:
From: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@fincentric.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tomng@fincentric.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry egress options for our on-prem deployment

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinCentric is very interested in Redwood's private offering. Our security team asked me to get concrete on observability: how do we get logs, metrics, and traces out of a private VPC/on-prem deployment into our SOC and Splunk instance?

Key constraints:
- No persistent outbound VPN to vendor-managed endpoints (customer controls egress).
- Support for mutual TLS (mTLS) and cert pinning is required by our security policy.
- We need custody/audit trail for the chain of delivery and proof of integrity.
- Retention and sampling controls should be configurable per-log type.

Questions we need answered for procurement:
1) What transport modes do you support (HEC over TLS, syslog over TLS, S3 drop via signed uploads, forwarder pull, etc.)?
2) For each mode, what firewall ports/IP ranges are required and can these be pinned to static egress IPs?
3) How are traces correlated with request IDs coming from the VPC workloads?
4) Example of artifacts we can ask our SIEM team to validate (sample payloads, headers, integrity checks).

I've attached a quick Telemetry Requirements spreadsheet with our baseline. Can you propose two recommended patterns (low-latency real-time vs air-gapped evidence bundle) and a short list of network controls we should plan for?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is on a 2-week window.

Best,
Leah Ortiz
Head of Security Operations
FinCentric

Attachment: telemetry-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 95KB)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@fincentric.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Mar 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry egress options for our on-prem deployment

Hi Leah — thanks for the clear list and attachment. Looping in Marissa (security/product) and Ben (on-prem engineering) to weigh in.

Executive summary / recommended patterns:

Pattern A — Real-time SIEM push (recommended for production monitoring)
- Mode: Splunk HEC / generic HTTPS endpoint over TLS with mTLS option.
- Flow: Collector deployed inside customer VPC (sidecar or host-level forwarder) -> outbound to customer-managed SIEM endpoint (HEC) OR outbound to a customer-provided collector in their DMZ.
- Benefits: Low latency, end-to-end encryption, can preserve trace IDs.
- Network needs: outbound HTTPS (443) to customer HEC; if Redwood must accept inbound we will require peered/private link (not preferred).
- IPs: We support static egress IPs when using Redwood-managed egress nodes in a Dedicated deployment; for Private/VPC option customers typically host the egress endpoint.

Pattern B — Periodic evidence bundles (air-gapped / compliance-friendly)
- Mode: Signed artifact uploads (S3-compatible with pre-signed URLs) or encrypted bundles transferred over an approved channel (scp/FTPS) to a customer-controlled staging host.
- Flow: Local forwarder collects and bundles logs, signs with customer/provided key, then pushes to staging provided by FinCentric or exports to removable media in fully air-gapped landings.
- Benefits: Auditability, custody proofs, good for regulated records.
- Network needs: Inbound/outbound depending on acceptance model; minimal continuous egress.

Tracing guidance:
- We can propagate and store request IDs and span IDs if your application injects them into requests entering the model runtime. Redwood's runtime will attach a deterministic trace header (X-Redwood-Trace) to generated responses so your tracing system can stitch LLM calls to upstream requests.
- For correlation into Splunk or Jaeger, we recommend including a small JSON field in logs with trace/span metadata; we can provide a mapping template.

Short list of firewall/tuning items (initial):
- Allow outbound 443 to your SIEM HEC host(s);
- If using mTLS, allow port 8443 or 443 depending on your endpoint config and ensure CA chain is installed on forwarder;
- If using pre-signed S3 artifacts, allow outbound to relevant S3 endpoints and to the staging host IP;
- DNS: forwarder needs to resolve customer endpoints and CRL/OCSP for cert validation.

Next steps:
1) Ben, Marissa — can you add a network-level checklist and a minimal sample manifest (HEC payload + headers) for Leah's team to validate?
2) Leah — if you can share a test HEC endpoint or a short window for a technical call this week, we can do validation with a small forwarder instance.

I attached a short PDF with the Private Observability options (redwood-priv-obsv-overview.pdf) and included a sample syslog line we use for SIEM mapping.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-priv-obsv-overview.pdf (PDF, 220KB); sample-syslog.log (text, 6KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@fincentric.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Mar 2029 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry egress options for our on-prem deployment

Adding a few technical precisions and a checklist — keeping it practical for their security team:

Network / egress specifics:
- Preferred ports: 443 (TLS), 8443 allowed for alternate mTLS. Avoid ephemeral high-numbered ports if customer egress ACLs are strict.
- IP design: If FinCentric requires static egress IPs for Redwood-managed egress nodes, we can provide a published set when using a Dedicated egress appliance. For pure customer-managed egress, advise creating a host in the DMZ with a small NAT pool and pin it in their firewall.
- Mutual TLS: support for client cert authentication and CRL/OCSP checks. Redwood can validate customer certs; customers can optionally pin our cert fingerprint for inbound configurations.

SIEM integration specifics (Splunk HEC example):
- HEC token + mTLS: use HEC token in header X-Splunk-Token plus mTLS at TLS layer for mutual trust.
- Body: JSON event per line, include fields: event_time, source_app, redwood_request_id, redwood_span_id, model_name, input_tokens, latency_ms.
- Sample header: Authorization: Splunk <token> ; Content-Type: application/json

Trace hooks and sampling:
- Default sampling: 1% for debug spans, 100% sampling option for emergency sessions (configurable per deployment).
- We can embed deterministic span IDs in token-level traces so that a single inference that fans out (multi-part prompts) keeps a single correlation ID.

Audit / proof of custody:
- For evidence bundles we recommend an envelope with: SHA256 manifest, signed manifest (customer key), and per-file checksums.
- We can provide a minimal verification script (shell + openssl) for FinCentric to validate uploads.

Checklist (deliverable for procurement):
- Provide test HEC host/credentials and a CIDR/IP allowlist window.
- Decide: Real-time HEC OR S3-signed-bundle. If HEC, provide token and preferred mTLS cert CN.
- Confirm retention SLA and purge window for logs forwarded to Redwood-managed stages.

I can prepare the HEC sample payload (headers + 3 event lines) and the openssl verification example by EOD. Ben, can you stub a forwarder container config with the minimal systemd unit + env vars for HEC URL and certs?

--
Marissa Cole
Product Security Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
